newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Bank of Scotland beats forecasts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bank of Scotland beats forecasts.

text.p: Bank of Scotland beat analysts' forecasts on Wednesday with a 22 percent rise in pre-tax profits for the year to the end of February and a larger than expected rise in its total dividend.
Pre-tax profits rose to 664.1 million pounds ($1.1 billion) compared to 545 million in the previous year while total dividend jumped 20 percent to 8.22p per share from 6.85p per share last time.
The top end of analysts' forecasts was for a profit of 660 million pounds, the figures helped by rather smaller than forecast bad debt provisions.
Bank of Scotland shares rose seven pence after the results were announced to a high of 345p but later fell back to stand a net 1p higher at 339p.
Bank Governor Sir Bruce Pattullo said in a statement that the rise in profits was based on the "ongoing development of the scope and professionalism of its businesses".
Taking out exceptional gains of 53.7 million pounds in the previous year's figures, Bank of Scotland said its pre-tax profit rise would have been an even healthier 27 percent.
Bank secretary David Hunter said in an interview that the Bank of Scotland would continue to improve its market share in niche businesses and by direct banking operations in England.

Analysts said the figures were solid, and were pleased by an easing of the cost to income ratio in the second half of the year compared to the first half and by continuing good asset quality despite the rise in lending volumes.
Inigo Edsberg at Panmure Gordon said the broker would continue with its "hold" recommendation believing that in yield terms other banks in the sector look more attractive.
But Hugh Pye of BZW, who continues to be a buyer of the shares, said they are undervalued and sees some upside to his fair-value estimate of 380 pence per share.
Analysts noted the rather disappointing contribution from Bank of Scotland's Australian unit BankWest, of which it owns 51.47 percent.
This year's figures included a full contribution for the first time from BankWest which made a profit of 71.6 million pounds.
BankWest said earlier that even this level of profit is unlikely to be sustained in the current year due to intense competition, lower lending rates and restructuring costs.

Hunter said margin pressure in the British market will also continue in the current year: "Our reaction to that is to make sure we are a low-cost provider. Any increase in costs is an increase in costs to produce future profit."
Hunter said Bank of Scotland would focus on organic growth. "We see tremendous opportunities in our UK and overseas business."
He said the Bank continues to be a growth story but conceded that many investors see growth as unfashionable because it has historically been equated with dangerous lending growth.

"We don't mind being unfashionable, we don't grow for its own sake, we want to add value for shareholders and the underlying quality of the assets shows we are growing the business in a balanced way," Hunter said. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
